title: Latency buckets, cost-aware panels, and investigation playbook
body:
Purpose:
This note proposes a compact, operator-friendly pattern for combining latency buckets with cost-aware dashboard panels and an investigation playbook for tokenized LLM inference. The goal is to help oncall and SRE quickly assess both user experience (p50/p95/p99) and economic impact (tokens/sec, estimated $/k tokens) when regressions occur.

Scope and motivation:
- Applies to token-serving inference endpoints (hosted + dedicated).
- Addresses common pain: tail latency spikes that do not correlate with obvious infra metrics, and the difficulty of understanding the cost tradeoffs of mitigations (e.g., increasing batch size vs turning on caching).
- Complementary to existing tracing and SLI work — focuses on dashboard composition and a short investigation checklist.

High-level design summary:
1) Latency buckets: capture request latency as histogram buckets aligned to decked sequence-length / prefix length categories. Buckets should be meaningful for UX: <50ms, 50-150ms, 150-500ms, 500-1s, 1-3s, >3s. Also maintain tokenized latency distributions (latency per token).
2) Cost-aware panels: show tokens/sec, tokens/response, estimated $/1k tokens (using current pricing model), and GPU-utilization-normalized cost. Correlate with model version and quantization profile.
3) Trace anchors: instrument traces with attributes that make attribution fast: request_id, model, model_variant, route, batch_size, seq_len, kv_cache_hit_rate, kv_cache_class (prefix vs partial), node_id, gpu_type, and allocator_wait_ms.
4) Investigation playbook: 6–8 step checklist for oncall to triage tail latency and cost anomalies.

Metric definitions (proposed canonical labels):
- inference_request_latency_ms_histogram: histogram of end-to-end latency (ingress -> final token sent). Buckets as above. Tag by model, route, customer_tier, and seq_len_bucket.
- latency_per_token_ms:{p50,p95,p99}: latency divided by actual token_count emitted.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: ratio of requests served from cache prefix hits vs total. Tag by model_variant and route.
- batch_size_distribution: histogram of batch sizes observed during serving.
- tokens_emitted_total: cumulative counter for tokens returned to callers.
- requests_total_by_model: standard request counter.
- estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: derived gauge that multiplies tokens_emitted rate by price_table[model_variant].
- gpu_efficiency: tokens_emitted / GPU-second (derived).
- allocator_wait_ms: time waiting for GPU memory allocator.

Suggested labels / attributes to attach to traces and metrics (consistent naming):
- request_id (string)
- trace_id (auto)
- model (string)
- model_variant (string)
- quant_profile (string)
- route (string)
- customer_id (string)
- batch_size (int)
- seq_len (int)
- token_count (int)
- kv_cache_hit (bool)
- kv_cache_prefetch (bool)
- node_id (string)
- gpu_type (string)
- allocator_wait_ms (int)
- response_size_bytes (int)

Tracing sampling rules (recommended):
- full-span traces for all requests with error codes or > p99 latency for that route (always).
- 1% sampled traces for normal traffic baseline.
- 10% sampling for requests with seq_len > 1024 or batch_size > 8.
- Dynamic bursts: raise sampling to 5% for routes flagged by active alerts.
- Store 72h of full traces for P0 routes, 24h for P1, and aggregated traces (span summaries) for others.

Dashboard panels (compact layout recommended: left column SLI + latency buckets, center column cost/connectivity, right column traces + drilldowns):
A. SLI + Latency Summary (top-left)
  - p50/p95/p99 latency time series by model (line chart).
  - latency histogram (stacked bar) with the latency buckets; ability to filter by seq_len_bucket.
  - latency per token trend (sparkline) for last 6h, 24h, 7d.
B. Cost & Throughput (top-center)
  - tokens/sec (rolling 1m) with tokens/response overlay.
  - estimated $/1k tokens (gauge + time series) with hoverable price breakdown per model_variant.
  - GPU tokens/sec per GPU panel (normalized) to reveal hotspots.
C. Cache & Batching (middle-left)
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio over time and by route.
  - batch_size_distribution heatmap (batch size vs time).
  - correlation scatter: batch_size vs latency_per_token with regression line.
D. Node / Infra (middle-right)
  - allocator_wait_ms by node_id (bar).
  - GPU utilization + memory pressure (stacked).
  - network egress (MB/s) per node.
E. Traces & Drilldowns (bottom-right)
  - trace-sampler quick links: show 10 most recent full traces for p99 spikes.
  - common-span-duration table: percentiles of key spans (tokenize, model_forward, kv_lookup, send_tokens).
F. Incident Quick-Checks (small widget)
  - single-click runbook buttons: "collect-session-samples", "increase-sampling", "isolate-model-variant" (these trigger internal ops endpoints).

Example PromQL / SQL snippets (copy into dashboard templating):
PromQL (tokens/sec):
  rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])
PromQL (p99 latency per route):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_ms_histogram_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
PromQL (kv hit ratio):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[5m])) by (route)
BigQuery (join trace attributes to request table example):
  SELECT
    r.request_id, r.model_variant, r.seq_len, t.span_name, t.duration_ms
  FROM `redwood-prod.traces.requests` r
  LEFT JOIN `redwood-prod.traces.spans` t ON r.trace_id = t.trace_id
  WHERE r.event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 6 HOUR)
    AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    AND r.latency_ms > 1000
  ORDER BY r.latency_ms DESC
  LIMIT 200

Alerting and thresholds (initial proposals):
- Alert A1 (P0): p99 latency for critical routes > 3s sustained for 2 minutes.
- Alert A2 (P1): kv_cache_hit_ratio drops below 50% for more than 5 minutes for any customer_tier=paid route.
- Alert A3 (P1): tokens/sec per GPU drops by 40% vs rolling 1h baseline while requests remain steady (possible mis-sharding).
- Alert A4 (P2): allocator_wait_ms p95 > 100ms for any node for 10 minutes.

Investigation playbook (quick steps):
1) Check SLI panel: confirm whether regression is latency (p99) or throughput (tokens/sec) related.
2) Look at latency buckets histogram: identify whether tail is new (more >3s) or baseline shifted.
3) Inspect batch_size heatmap and kv_cache_hit_ratio to see if more cold starts / smaller batches occurred.
4) Open the list of recent full traces for p99 spikes; prioritize traces with high allocator_wait_ms or large model_forward spans.
5) Run BigQuery join (example above) to get top offending request_ids and attach to incident.
6) Consider temporary mitigations: enable cache prefetch for specific prefixes, throttle background load, revert model_variant, or increase prewarm pool. Evaluate cost impact using cost panels.
7) After mitigation, keep elevated trace sampling for 1–6 hours and capture any regression fingerprints for postmortem.

Dashboard UX & performance notes:
- Prefer compact widgets and shareable links that pre-populate route/model variables.
- Limit high-cardinality dimensions by default (customer_id not shown unless drilling).
- Store downsampled rollups for 90d retention to keep dashboards responsive.

Operational constraints and cost tradeoffs:
- Higher trace sampling increases storage costs linearly. Use adaptive sampling with short windows.
- Full-span capture for large seq_len is high-value; restrict to small percent and rotate sampling policies per incident.
- Derived metrics (estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens) should be computed in a lightweight stream job (not BigQuery) for near-real-time display.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define seq_len_bucket boundaries for multi-model environment (action: product/solutions to propose mapping).
- Finalize price_table ingestion source and cadence for model variants.
- Add example Grafana dashboard json export and templated panels (action: Diego to prototype).
- Validate allocator_wait_ms instrumentation across all runtime languages (Samir).

References and context links:
- OBS-412 (investigate tokenized p99 regressions around 2024-10)
- confluence:obs-dashboard-patterns (patterns + previous experiments)
- github telemetry PR 198 (metric name changes proposed)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep histogram buckets coarse; we want signal, not noise.
- Emphasize correlating cost panels with mitigation options to make runbook decisions measurable.
- This doc intentionally compact — next step is a one-pager playbook for oncall and a sample dashboard JSON.
